meta: Jesus talks with his mother as the astonished host tastes the water turned to wine in Giuseppe Maria Crespi's Wedding at Cana, about 1686.
about: Giuseppe Maria Crespi filled this wedding feast, where Jesus worked his first miracle, with luxurious accessories and small exchanges between the figures. On the left Jesus talks with his mother. On the right the astonished host and his servant taste the water Jesus has turned into wine. The museum says the painting joins the Venetian tradition of color and grandeur with the close observation of people typical of Crespi's native Bologna.

meta: A travelling family with a chained bear, a loaded horse and a foal on a country road, painted by Karel Frederik Bombled in 1881.
about: A travelling family walks along a country road with a bear on a lead, a loaded horse and a foal. The Rijksmuseum notes that they may be a Roma family. Karel Frederik Bombled painted it in 1881.

meta: Aglaida and her slave Boniface, living as pagan sinners in Rome around 290, painted by Alexandre Cabanel about 1857.
about: Alexandre Cabanel, a favorite of Napoleon III and a leader of the academic style with its precise drawing and smooth modeling, painted the wealthy Roman Aglaida and her concubine slave Boniface, who live as pagan sinners in Rome around 290. On a trip to Tarsus, Boniface became a Christian and was tortured and beheaded. Aglaida also converted, gave all her goods to the poor and built a church for his relics.

meta: A candlestick design with a foot of auricular animals and torch-bearing children, by Jan Lutma, about 1630.
about: This is a candlestick design seen from the front. The tripartite foot is made of animals in the auricular style, with children standing on it, each carrying a lighted torch. The child at the left also holds a bowl and the one at the right a drinking vessel. The shaft is a seated child with a torch in the left hand and a bowl held up by the right hand and head. Jan Lutma made the design.

meta: A tournament and hunters in a landscape painted on poplar by Jan van Scorel in Italy, 1519 to 1520.
about: Jan van Scorel was one of the first northern European artists to make a long trip to Italy to study antiquities and the new Renaissance style. This landscape must date from his time in southern Europe, since the panel is poplar, a wood common in Italy. Jousting and hunting were frequent themes in northern landscapes, especially prints, and Italian patrons were drawn to these lavish visions of court life.

meta: Diana hunts with two nymphs and hounds in a landscape by Abraham Genoels, about 1685, a pendant picture.
about: In a landscape the goddess Diana goes hunting with two nymphs and hunting dogs. Abraham Genoels painted it in 1685 as a pendant to another picture in the Rijksmuseum, which holds both.

meta: Sebastiano del Piombo's Saint Dorothy, or Young Roman Woman with a Fruit Basket, painted about 1512 and long given to Raphael.
about: Saint Dorothy, also called Young Roman Woman with a Fruit Basket, is an oil on panel of about 1512 by Sebastiano del Piombo, now in the Gemäldegalerie in Berlin. A basket is an attribute of Saint Dorothy, which gave it its first title. He painted it in Rome, after being summoned in August 1511 to join Agostino Chigi's decoration of the Villa Farnesina. It was long wrongly given to Raphael until Gustav Friedrich Waagen revived the right attribution in 1835.

meta: Hunters with dogs in a wooded hilly landscape, painted by Jacob Esselens about 1660.
about: This is a wooded, hilly landscape with a few hunters and dogs in the foreground. Jacob Esselens painted it, and the catalog dates it to 1660. The Rijksmuseum holds it, and its note says nothing more.

meta: Saul and his men cower as the ghost of Samuel rises in William Sidney Mount's Saul and the Witch of Endor.
about: William Sidney Mount painted only a few historical and literary scenes. This one illustrates a passage from the Hebrew Bible in which Saul sought help from an oracle before going to war with the Philistines. The witch called up the spirit of the prophet Samuel so that Saul could ask his advice. Saul and his men cower in horror as the ghost comes forward to speak. The episode was familiar to 19th-century audiences raised on scripture.

meta: The Countess, an unfinished, sketchy portrait by Emanuel Gottlieb Leutze, painted when he was an itinerant portraitist in 1838.
about: Emanuel Leutze concentrated on the handsome, serious features of his sitter. The sketchy, unfinished handling shows him working out details, as do the outlined hands. He was an itinerant portraitist in 1838, and the inscription below the portrait shows he painted it in a friend's studio or a rented space. The museum says the rich brushwork and colors reflect two popular Philadelphia portraitists, Thomas Sully and Gilbert Stuart.

meta: Saint Peter kneels before Saint Paul as the Trinity appears on clouds, a sketch by Gaetano Gandolfi, about 1770.
about: This sketch shows the kneeling Saint Peter revering Saint Paul, who stands leaning on his sword with his left hand on a book held by a seated child, as he looks up at the Trinity on the clouds. An angel stands behind Peter and raises the keys in his left hand. At the left stands Faith or Religion, a woman with the cross, a chalice and the Host. Gaetano Gandolfi made it.

meta: Giovanni Fattori's Cousin Argia of 1861, an early Macchiaioli work labeled as a gift to a cousin no one can identify.
about: Cousin Argia is an 1861 oil on card by Giovanni Fattori, now in the Gallery of Modern Art in Florence. A label on the back says it is from Giovanni Fattori to his dear cousin Argia, in 1861, but it may not be in his hand and no Argia is known in his family. Wikipedia calls it one of his first significant works, in which his academic training gives way to the new Macchiaioli approach.

meta: Sano di Pietro's Nativity of the Virgin of 1438 to 1439, the central panel of a Siena altarpiece.
about: Nativity of the Virgin is a tempera on panel of 1438 to 1439, now in the Museum of Sacred Art in Asciano, Tuscany. It is the central panel of a multi-panel altarpiece whose other panels show episodes from the life of the Virgin Mary. Roberto Longhi and others once gave it to the Master of the Osservanza Triptych, but it is now usually attributed to Sano di Pietro.

meta: The International Indian Council of 1843 at Tahlequah, painted by John Mix Stanley, who was there.
about: In the mid-nineteenth century the United States government moved tribes from the Southeast to Indian Territory, later Oklahoma and Kansas. In 1843 the Cherokee principal chief John Ross called a meeting of the tribes at Tahlequah to renew their ancient customs and alliances. Hundreds of Native Americans came, with several United States officials. The artist John Mix Stanley was there.

meta: A Daoist and a crane in an autumn landscape from Chen Hongshou's double album of paintings after ancient masters.
about: The twenty paintings of this double album by Chen Hongshou include landscapes and figures as well as flowers, plus one leaf with a woman, a subject not found in the other albums of his later career. The museum calls his late works summations of his quirky, archaistic, hyper-refined art without shallowness or sentimentality. His figures and landscapes there are miniaturized, like small Chinese gardens. This leaf shows a Daoist and a crane in an autumn landscape.

meta: Jefferson Davis in Mathew B. Brady's studio portrait of about 1860, titled Our First President Quickstep.
about: Jefferson Davis, who would become the Confederacy's only president, entered politics in 1845 when Mississippians elected him to Congress. He gave up the seat to fight in the Mexican-American War, then served as a U.S. senator and as Franklin Pierce's secretary of war. He championed Southern economic and political interests and was an outspoken defender of chattel slavery, yet he opposed breaking up the Union. Mathew B. Brady made this portrait.

meta: A woman on a balcony above a busy street in Umberto Boccioni's Futurist painting The Street Enters the House, 1911 to 1912.
about: The Street Enters the House is an oil on canvas by Umberto Boccioni in the Futurist style. It centers on a woman on a balcony in front of a busy street, with the sounds of the activity below shown as a riot of shapes and colors. Boccioni was one of the founders of Futurism. It was first shown in Paris in 1912 at the first Futurist exhibition, and it is now in the Sprengel Museum in Hanover.

meta: Rachel Ruysch's flower piece of roses, convolvulus and poppies in an urn on a stone ledge, painted in 1688.
about: Roses, Convolvulus, Poppies and Other Flowers in an Urn on a Stone Ledge is an oil on canvas of 1688 by the Dutch painter Rachel Ruysch, and an example of Dutch Golden Age painting. It is in the National Museum of Women in the Arts in Washington. Ruysch is recorded as making pendant paintings, one of flowers, called a bloemstuk, and one of fruit, called a fruitstuk, but no pendant to this one is known.
